<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD contains only standard variable definitions and two top-level loops that execute during sourcing. The first loop iterates over a hardcoded `_languages` array to dynamically append to `pkgname`/`source` arrays and uses `eval` to define per-language package functions. The second loop builds the `noextract` array from the `source` array. All data is static/hardcoded in the PKGBUILD itself — no command substitution, network access, file reads, or external input occurs at top level. The `eval` is a code smell but operates solely on trusted, static array data to generate repetitive function definitions, a common pattern for split-language packages. No malicious behavior executes during `makepkg --printsrcinfo`.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>Top-level code only defines variables and generates functions from hardcoded data; no execution risk.</summary>
</security_assessment>
